svg.title: The MARS agent loop: how a language model's tool calls are checked, run and recorded
svg.desc: A ring of five steps sits at the centre: propose, validate, approve, execute and observe, one pass per tool call and at most 20 turns. On the left, a language model from any provider (Claude, GPT, Gemini, or Ollama locally) proposes a tool call and receives a structured result. On the right, 55 tested tools in five groups run the call; the same tools are served over MCP. Four numbered call-outs show real traffic produced by MARS: a proposed call to compute_pulsar_periodogram; a call caught by validation as stringified_null; a download that needs a person's approval (risk tags slow, writes); and the structured result, a period of 0.71462 s. Below, every pass is written to the session record, and a benchmark of 144 recorded sessions reports the share of correct answers per model with 95% intervals.
